steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Narrative writing tells a story with a beginning, middle, and end. It features characters, a plot with events, a setting, and often explores themes through conflict and resolution.

steps.title: The Five-Part Structure
steps.body: Exposition: Introduce characters, setting, situation Rising Action: Build tension through complications Climax: The turning point or peak of tension Falling Action: Consequences of the climax Resolution: Loose ends tied up, new equilibrium

steps.title: Show Character Through Action
steps.body: Instead of telling us someone is brave, show them facing fear. Instead of telling us someone is kind, show them helping another character.

steps.title: Dialogue Rules
steps.body: Each character should have a distinct voice Keep it realistic - people interrupt, trail off, use incomplete sentences Avoid info-dumps - don't use dialogue to explain the plot Use action beats instead of endless "he said, she said"

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What are the five parts of a classic story arc? | What does "in medias res" mean and why is it effective? | Name two ways to reveal character without directly stating traits.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Exposition (introduction), Rising Action (complications), Climax (turning point), Falling Action (consequences), Resolution (conclusion). | "In medias res" means starting in the middle of the action. It's effective because it immediately grabs the reader's attention and creates intrigue from the first line. | Through dialogue (how they speak), through actions (what they do), through reactions (how they respond to events), through interactions with others, through telling details of appearance or behaviour.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Plan before you write - know your beginning, middle, and end Focus on ONE key incident - don't try to cover too much Start with impact - hook the reader immediately Show character through action and dialogue, not description Use short sentences to build tension in key moments Include a turning point - something must change End with resonance - leave a final impression Leave time to check spelling and punctuation
